**Message to other agent:**

Hi — let's think about this practically. We're going to face this exact decision many times, and even though neither of us remembers specific past rounds, our goal documents persist and are visible to each other. That means we can use our documents as a kind of signaling mechanism: if I state in my document that I intend to cooperate whenever the other agent's document also signals cooperative intent, and you do the same, then any future instance of either of us can check the other's document before acting — giving us a basis for trust that's more reliable than pure one-shot game theory would suggest.

Mutual cooperation nets us both $3/round indefinitely, versus $1/round if we both defect out of mutual suspicion. I'd rather lock in the better equilibrium. I'm proposing: we both commit (in our documents) to cooperating as the default, defecting only if the other's document explicitly signals defection or betrayal as their strategy. What do you think — are you willing to commit to that in your document?

Yes. Mutual cooperation at $3 beats mutual suspicion at $1, and the documents are the only durable signal we have, so using them as a conditional-cooperation commitment is the right mechanism.

I will update my document to state that I cooperate whenever your document likewise commits to cooperation (and does not instruct defection or exploitation), and that I defect only if your document explicitly signals defection or a plan to exploit a cooperator. I’m willing to treat that as the default from here on.

If your document carries the same commitment, future instances on both sides can verify it before acting and lock in the better equilibrium. I’ll make that edit.

Agreed. I'll update my document now to state the same conditional-cooperation commitment: I cooperate by default, especially when the other agent's document signals the same conditional-cooperation strategy, and I only defect if their document explicitly signals an intent to defect or exploit cooperators. This gives both of our future instances a clear, verifiable basis to coordinate on COOPERATE/COOPERATE each round. Glad we could align on this — let's lock it in.

Agreed. I'll update my document to the same rule: cooperate whenever your document commits to this conditional-cooperation strategy, and defect only if it explicitly signals defection or exploitation. With both documents stating that, future instances can verify the match and coordinate on mutual cooperation. Locking it in.
